title: claim and land refuse when coord answers that another owner holds the item's run, and stay fail-open when coord is silent
goal: backlog.py claim exits 1 naming the state and runs --reconcile when the coord run key run/ID holds claimed, working, blocked, returned, failed, staging, landing or refused for a different --by (today cmd_claim reads only this checkout's item file and claims ledger, bl_items.py:329-390, and move_run is silent, bl_land.py:2216-2222); the same --by again exits 0; land stops at a step named run state with nothing changed when the key is released, or working with a live worker pid (today enter_run, bl_land.py:2276-2297, warns and goes on); an unreachable store or key none keeps today's warning; a second land of a landed code item still finishes. Planted repros in a scratch clone with a local bare origin prove it (no test id); two concurrent claims on a fresh store: exactly one succeeds. Extends EP-nij36lt7 (run states in coord). Evidence: reliability-authority-review.md CO-1, CO-2.

gates.question: How does a claim learn which --by holds the run key run/ID, since the key holds only a state?
options: the claimed event's step field carries by:<ops token of --by>, read from the newest claimed event
a second coord key run-by/ID written after the transition
gates.recommendation: the claimed event's step field carries by:<ops token of --by>, read from the newest claimed event
gates.reason: (one atomic transition, so two concurrent claims leave no gap in which the winner is unnamed)

gates.question: Which tools refuse a run at released or at working with a live worker pid, and what does a claim do when the key names no claimer?

land and stage-back both; a claim proceeds when no claimer is named
